title: Arrays & Strings Journey
description: Array updates, hashing, prefix sums, two pointers, sliding windows, and matrix traversal.

journey.outcome: Choose a scanning invariant and the smallest useful state instead of repeatedly rescanning an array or string.

connections.remove-element: Begin with separate read and write positions. The processed prefix contains exactly the values kept so far, even when the input array is modified in place.
connections.remove-duplicates-from-sorted-array: Keep the read/write invariant but use sorted order to recognize duplicates locally. Compare against the last retained value rather than building a second collection.
connections.move-zeroes: Preserve the relative order of retained values while moving rejected zeroes to the suffix. This adds a stable-order requirement to the same compaction technique.
connections.contains-duplicate: Now sorted order is unavailable. A set remembers earlier values so each arrival can be checked without scanning the entire processed prefix.
connections.valid-anagram: A set loses multiplicity, so replace membership with character counts. Equality of frequency tables captures the relationship without depending on original order.
connections.two-sum: Store a useful lookup key rather than every possible pair. Each value asks whether its complement has appeared, and indices must come from two distinct positions.
connections.group-anagrams: Promote the anagram frequency signature into a grouping key. Many pairwise comparisons become one hash lookup per word, with a collision-free signature representation.
connections.longest-consecutive-sequence: Use the set to identify sequence starts, not merely neighbors. Iterate unique values and only expand from a value whose predecessor is absent to avoid repeated walks.
connections.majority-element: Frequency counting supplies a direct solution; the strict majority guarantee also permits pair cancellation with one candidate and a balance counter. State the guarantee before using that shortcut.
connections.encode-and-decode-strings: Move from comparing string signatures to preserving exact string boundaries. An unambiguous length-prefixed format can represent separators inside words and empty strings without losing information.
connections.find-the-index-of-the-first-occurrence-i: Now compare a pattern against consecutive text positions. After a partial match fails, KMP's prefix table reuses a suffix that is also a pattern prefix instead of restarting every comparison.
connections.product-of-array-except-self: Replace repeated exclusion scans with prefix and suffix summaries. Combining the two sides answers each position without division and naturally handles zeroes.
connections.maximum-subarray: Summarize the useful history in one best-ending-here value. A harmful prefix can be discarded, while a separate best-so-far value records the global answer.
connections.count-subarrays-with-given-sum: Use differences between prefix sums to describe every subarray. A frequency map counts earlier prefixes that would make the current interval sum equal the target.
connections.largest-subarray-with-sum-0: Reuse prefix differences, but store the earliest index instead of a frequency. Equal prefix sums bound a zero-sum interval, and the earliest occurrence maximizes its length.
connections.valid-palindrome: Move to two ends of the same sequence. Skip characters outside the comparison rule and shrink the unchecked interval only after its endpoints agree.
connections.two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted: Replace Two Sum's hash map with sorted-order decisions. If the endpoint sum is too small or too large, one pointer movement eliminates a provably useless candidate.
connections.3sum: Fix one value, then reuse the sorted two-pointer pair solver on the suffix. Deduplicate both the fixed value and successful pairs without removing legitimate combinations.
connections.container-with-most-water: Keep two endpoints, but optimize an area rather than an exact sum. Moving the taller wall cannot improve the current limiting height, which justifies discarding the shorter wall.
connections.maximum-average-subarray-i: Start sliding windows with a fixed width. Add the entering value and subtract the leaving value instead of recomputing every window sum.
connections.longest-substring-without-repeating-char: Let the window width vary while preserving a validity condition. Move its left edge until the incoming character no longer duplicates one already inside.
connections.minimum-size-subarray-sum: Change the objective from the longest valid window to the shortest window reaching a sum. Positivity makes shrinking and expanding monotonic; negative values would invalidate this reasoning.
connections.permutation-in-string: Combine fixed-size windows with anagram frequency counts. A window is a permutation only when its multiplicities match, not just its distinct characters.
connections.longest-repeating-character-replacement: Measure invalidity as window length minus the most frequent character count. The replacement budget determines whether the current window can be made uniform.
connections.minimum-window-substring: Combine variable-width shrinking with required multiplicities. Track how many requirements are satisfied and shrink only while the whole target remains covered.
connections.rotate-image: Extend in-place reasoning to two dimensions. A transpose followed by row reversal expresses a clockwise rotation without assigning over values that are still needed.
connections.spiral-matrix: Replace pointer endpoints with four shrinking boundaries. Finish one edge at a time and recheck boundaries before traversing the opposite edge of a thin remainder.
connections.set-matrix-zeroes: Use existing matrix cells as compact marker storage. Separate the first row and column's original state so markers do not destroy the information they represent.
connections.game-of-life: The next state depends on the entire previous generation. Encode old and new cell states separately during an in-place pass so earlier writes cannot affect later neighbor counts.
